record.paper_title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions
record.original_question: Let C be a polycyclic code whose generator polynomial g(x) divides a trinomial x^n - a x^i - b over a finite field, with n prime. Is it always true that C cannot be dual-containing?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.11. A polycyclic code is not dual-containing if the generator polynomial g|x^n - axi - b, where n is prime.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and let $n$ be a prime number. Consider a trinomial of the form
$$f(x) = x^n - a x^i - b \in \mathbb{F}_q[x],$$
where $a, b \in \mathbb{F}_q$ and $1 \le i \le n-1$. Let $g(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ be a monic divisor of $f(x)$, and let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be the polycyclic code of length $n$ associated with $f(x)$ whose generator polynomial is $g(x)$; that is, $C$ is the image of the ideal $(g(x))/(f(x))$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]/(f(x))$ under the coordinate identification with $\mathbb{F}_q^n$. Let
$$C^{\perp} = \{ u \in \mathbb{F}_q^n : \langle u, c\rangle = 0 \text{ for all } c \in C\}$$
denote the Euclidean dual of $C$ with respect to the standard inner product. Prove or disprove: under the above hypotheses (in particular, $n$ prime), the code $C$ is never dual-containing, i.e. $C^{\perp} \not\subseteq C$ unless $C$ is trivial in the excluded sense.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in the work introducing polycyclic codes associated to trinomials. Follow-up works (e.g., subsequent arXiv papers extending the theory to chain rings and studying duality of polycyclic codes) continue to investigate trinomial-based polycyclic codes but do not appear to resolve this specific conjecture. No explicit proof or counterexample is found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: presents several conjectures about polycyclic codes associated with trinomials
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: On polycyclic linear and additive codes associated to a trinomial over a finite chain ring
status_evidence.snippet: investigates polycyclic codes associated with a trinomial of arbitrary degree n
status_evidence.claim: A 2025 follow-up paper extends the framework but does not explicitly resolve the dual-containing conjecture for prime n.
